problem: `create_app` installs Starlette's `TrustedHostMiddleware` with only `allowed_hosts` (ledger/api.py:735-736), so the middleware keeps its default www-redirect behaviour: with `allowed_hosts=["www.dashboard.example"]`, a request whose Host is `dashboard.example` is not rejected but answered with a 307 redirect to `http://www.dashboard.example/...`, contradicting the README "Production" section (README.md:272) and the `create_app` docstring (ledger/api.py:539-541), which promise 400 `Invalid host header` for every Host that is not one of the names. Only a host with no www counterpart (e.g. `evil.example`) gets the documented 400 today.
api_behavior: The documented `TrustedHostMiddleware` takes a `www_redirect` argument that is on by default and turns a non-www host into a redirect to its www counterpart; hosts that do not validate are the ones that get a 400. So the redirect is the documented default behaviour of the middleware that `create_app` currently uses without that argument, and the documented way to get the 400 instead is to pass `www_redirect=False`. Allowed hosts are matched by name, with `*.example.com` style wildcards for subdomains, so turning the redirect off does not change name or wildcard matching. FastAPI's `app.add_middleware(...)` accepts such keyword arguments for the middleware class, and the middleware added last stays the outermost, so the existing position of the call (added last in `create_app`) keeps the current order.
recommended_change: In ledger/api.py, change the middleware registration to `app.add_middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=list(allowed_hosts), www_redirect=False)` (keeping it added last and everything else, including `allowed_hosts=None` skipping the middleware, as it is). Nothing else in the code needs to change; the README and docstring already describe the wanted 400 behaviour.

sources.quote: www_redirect - If set to True, requests to non-www versions of the allowed hosts will be redirected to their www counterparts. Defaults to True.
If an incoming request does not validate correctly then a 400 response will be sent.
allowed_hosts - A list of domain names that should be allowed as hostnames. Wildcard domains such as *.example.com are supported for matching subdomains.

When you add multiple middlewares using either @app.middleware() decorator or app.add_middleware() method, each new middleware wraps the application, forming a stack. The last middleware added is the outermost, and the first is the innermost.

uncertainties: The middleware page at starlette.dev/middleware/ is the current documentation and is not pinned to the installed starlette 1.8.0; it also documents features from later releases (the release notes page shows 1.10.0 as the newest), so I cannot quote a 1.8.0-specific page for `www_redirect`. The 1.8.0 release-notes entry does not announce any change to `www_redirect`, and it is not listed as removed in 1.0/1.8.0, but the docs page itself does not name a version.
The documentation does not give the exact 400 body text (`Invalid host header`); it only says a 400 response is sent. That body text comes from the repository's README, not from the quoted docs.
The documentation does not spell out every matching detail (e.g. how ports in the Host header or a literal `*` entry are treated); it only states name matching plus `*.example.com` wildcards.
